### MCP Server & Brain Query Layer  [id: c03233e5-6a19-44fd-a5f5-3d4ccd3351f5]
A Model Context Protocol server that exposes accumulated brain knowledge to AI agents, enabling new sessions to query features, insights, and patterns rather than exploring the codebase from scratch.
- The MCP server predated the spec that proposed building one, with a sophisticated file-based implementation reading from .repo/ alongside an online REST implementation querying the DB directly — two complementary approaches coexisting. [s:3977fef3] The Brain API was discovered to be 'two APIs in a trenchcoat' — four tools speaking the retired Topic ontology and three speaking Feature from Postgres with no shared ids — which was resolved by unifying entirely around Feature keys in the v1.1 contract, with Topic tools and proposeKnowledgeDelta removed. [s:348dbc5a] MCP-to-session correlation uses explicit stamping (tools take an optional sessionId and the server stamps it), and no MCP call was emitting activity events until instrumentation was added, meaning Brain was previously blind to its own usage. [s:348dbc5a]

### Activity Event Backbone  [id: 1bc74e71-4587-45fb-94b7-4f830c7d8022]
A freeform, self-contained event table that acts as the observability index layer for all pipeline and MCP activity, with repo/branch/worktree as top-level columns to support parallel worktree session
- The daemon's live ObservedEvent stream and the DB schema's rawEvents/normalizedEvents were discovered to be completely separate pipelines with no connection, establishing the need for a unified event backbone. [s:2b589b44] The activity event table uses fully freeform categories, tags, and actor values — no enums, no taxonomy — with source_type/source_id back-references to originating records, and repo/branch/worktree as top-level columns; the embedding column is deferred as TEXT until pgvector is ready. [s:138200f0] Event emission follows the pattern of importing `emitEvents` and `ActivityEvent`, building events with freeform fields, and always wrapping in try/catch so failures never propagate to the parent operation; context fields (repo, branch, worktree) are auto-carried. [s:8e312af2]

### Dashboard UI & Journal  [id: c41bdbbb-483b-457a-a510-35155de46e29]
A React single-page application serving as the human-facing surface of the brain, featuring a journal-as-river primary view, feature detail pages, a review queue, and a Correspondence chat system — al
- The ink-and-paper editorial design system (Newsreader font, timeline spine, paper grain, night-desk dark mode, native elements over shadcn) was established as the visual language for the entire application, with the Journal as the default landing page. [s:348dbc5a] The journal-as-river model was chosen over a Notion-style Knowledge Tree after recognizing the tree metaphor existed only in the UI and export layer — the underlying data model (activity_events as backbone, Features as lenses) was already a graph/river. [s:72b991b8] The Correspondence chat system uses data-talk HTML attributes for zero-import page-element context pinning so any future surface gets chat capability for free, and the UI follows a lens architecture where the same provenance chain serves C-level health views and engineer evidence drill-downs. [s:72b991b8][s:38a57241]

### Digest Pipeline & Understanding Stage  [id: 9e23fadf-7d34-49aa-87bd-e741ad09d84e]
The core ingestion pipeline that reads raw session transcripts, extracts moments, classifies exchanges, and produces structured understanding (insights, patterns, confidence) stored in the database. E
- The pipeline processes sessions through stages including moment extraction, classification, and brain synthesis, with LLM-backed tasks governed by EDD and mechanical tasks by TDD. [s:3977fef3] A major fidelity audit revealed that 101 of 102 evidence rows contained a fallback value due to a Zod schema default, and a lost-tail bug caused ~7.7 hours of one session to be missing from its digest — driving a full understanding-stage rewrite. [s:38a57241] The committed digestion topology is two-phase deliberative reading (Phase 1 draft with provisional commits, Phase 2 retrospective revision where only revised claims pass the commit gate), with LangGraph StateGraph as the agent loop substrate and derived confidence replacing model-emitted confidence. [s:38a57241]

### Agentic Team Loop & Workflow Orchestration  [id: 5ace2e20-0e5b-41b6-b0b6-aa8f3c67fe0e]
A workflow-backed parallel agent execution system using git worktrees, human gates on consequential actions, and handoff artifacts — enabling multi-workstream development where the dev loop dogfoods t
- The team loop uses parallel worktree agents (Option A) with human gates on consequential actions; three of four Iteration 1 worktrees were silently created from a stale ancestor rather than HEAD, making merges unsafe — a base-integrity bug that the human gate caught before anything landed on the branch. [s:c1de9b9b] WS-A owns all schema and migrations while downstream workstreams build against a pinned contract, and the parallel multi-agent build with a pinned API contract produced zero field-name or shape mismatches between independently-built components, validating the contract-first approach. [s:c1de9b9b][s:348dbc5a] Agentic handoffs should be mindset-only with open questions rather than templates, to preserve reviewer independence and avoid anchoring the receiving agent to the sender's solution. [s:c1de9b9b]

### Storage Schema & Migration Infrastructure  [id: 8256bd6d-0698-4606-8879-da0016249ee6]
The Drizzle ORM schema defining all database tables (features, activity_events, moments, brain hierarchy) and the migration chain that keeps the Postgres database in sync with the TypeScript source of
- Adding new InsightCategory values requires an explicit Drizzle migration because the enum is DB-backed, not just a TypeScript type change; the drizzle-kit journal lost track of previously manually applied migrations, causing regeneration of already-applied schema changes. [s:3977fef3][s:138200f0] The 8-migration chain was discovered to be broken because drizzle-kit migrate uses timestamp comparison only with no per-file hashing, causing migrations with wrong or duplicate timestamps to be silently skipped on a fresh database — the entire chain was scrapped in favor of a single clean baseline migration from schema.ts as source of truth. [s:72b991b8] The schema is now Feature-centric with the Topic subsystem fully excised, activity_events as the backbone index layer, and the 26 pre-existing tsc errors as the binding baseline that all new work must not increase. [s:72b991b8][s:348dbc5a]
